title: Convexity of Radial Mean Bodies via an Extension of Ball's Bodies
summary: In this work, we extend a classical theorem of Keith Ball on integrals of log-concave functions along rays against the weight $r^{p-1}$ to the previously inaccessible regime $p\in (-1,0)$: if $g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+$ is an integrable, upper semi-continuous, log-concave function which attains its maximum at the origin, then \[ x\mapsto \left(\frac{p}{g(o)}\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{p-1}(g(rx)-g(o))\mathrm{d}\,r\right)^{-\frac{1}{p}} \] is a positively 1-homogeneous convex function on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Our approach also provides a new proof of the original regime $p> 0$. The argument is based on a…
